hints: Start by drawing out 2-methylbut-1-ene and look carefully at what is attached to each carbon of the C=C double bond.
Remember that for E/Z isomerism each C of the double bond must have two different groups, but C1 here is $\text{CH}_2$ with two identical H atoms.
For HBr addition, think Markovnikov: H adds to the carbon already rich in H, so Br ends up on the more substituted carbon to give the more stable carbocation.
walkthrough:
**Draw the alkene structure**

Let's see what we are working with. 2-methylbut-1-ene is $\text{CH}_2=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$.

The double bond is between C1 and C2. C1 has two H atoms, C2 has a $\text{CH}_3$ group and a $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ group.

**Test Student 1: geometrical isomers?**

For cis-trans or E/Z isomerism, each carbon of the C=C must be joined to two different groups. Restricted rotation alone is not enough.

Rule check:
$$\text{geometrical isomerism needs } >\text{C}(X)(Y) \text{ and } >\text{C}(P)(Q) \text{ with } X \neq Y, P \neq Q$$
Here C1 is $\text{CH}_2$, so X = Y = H. Swapping the two H atoms makes no difference, so no geometrical isomers exist. Student 1 is wrong.

**Test Student 2: HBr addition product?**

Alkenes undergo electrophilic addition with HBr. The major product follows Markovnikov's rule, via the more stable carbocation.

$$\text{CH}_2=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{HBr} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3-\text{CBr}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
H adds to C1 (the carbon with more H atoms) to form a tertiary carbocation at C2, then $\text{Br}^-$ attacks to give 2-bromo-2-methylbutane as the main product, not 1-bromo-2-methylbutane. Student 2 is wrong.

**Conclude**

Since both statements are incorrect, neither student is correct.

options.A: Incorrect. This would require both statements to be true. Student 1 fails because C1 has two identical H atoms, and Student 2 fails because Markovnikov addition gives the 2-bromo product, not the 1-bromo product.
options.B: Incorrect. Student 1 alone is not correct. Many students think any alkene with a double bond shows geometrical isomerism, but 2-methylbut-1-ene has $\text{CH}_2=$ at one end, so E/Z isomerism is impossible.
options.C: Incorrect. Student 2 alone is not correct. 1-bromo-2-methylbutane is the anti-Markovnikov product. The H of HBr adds to C1 and Br adds to the more substituted C2, giving 2-bromo-2-methylbutane as the major product via a tertiary carbocation.
options.D: Correct. Student 1 is wrong because no geometrical isomers are possible, and Student 2 is wrong because the main Markovnikov product is 2-bromo-2-methylbutane. Therefore neither student is correct.
